signals.source_text: On September 8, DIU and Honeywell Aerospace flight-tested a quantum magnetic navigation (MagNav) system on an Embraer 170, flying GPS-off between Puget Sound and southern Alaska for 4 hours and 23 minutes. Result: 89% better position accuracy than legacy backup navigation. The more interesting fact is why that number holds instead of degrading. Inertial navigation — the usual GPS backup — accumulates error over time; every second without a fix adds to the drift, because it's dead reckoning from a last-known position. MagNav doesn't dead-reckon. It reads the Earth's crustal magnetic field, a fixed, unjammable feature layer, and matches against it the way terrain-relative navigation matches against elevation maps. Error doesn't compound with flight time — it resets with every good magnetic fix. That's a fundamentally different failure mode than the inertial and RF-based alt-PNT approaches most solicitations have funded, and it's why DIU moved this fast: problem-to-prototype in a matter of months, out of 72 companies that responded to the original solicitation. Next stop is a C-17 test later this year. If you're in the PNT space, the lesson isn't "add a magnetometer." It's that DIU will fund an entirely different error model — not just another sensor bolted onto the same inertial-drift architecture — when the physics genuinely changes the problem. #DoW #Defense #Autonomy #GPS -deniedNav

signals.source_text: Recently, I came across an insightful talk on Model-Based Design and GenAI by Avinash Nehemiah from MathWorks . The talk explored how GenAI is rapidly transforming engineering workflows and how the shift from AI tools to AI Agents could significantly improve engineering productivity. However, automotive engineering comes with unique challenges. A vehicle is not simply a software product; it is a complex, safety-critical, multi-domain system that interacts with the physical world. Therefore, challenges such as black-box behavior, non-deterministic outputs, traceability gaps, inconsistent quality, and scalability remain important considerations. One of the key themes of the talk was finding the right balance between automotive engineering discipline and the opportunities offered by GenAI. Combining Trusted Tools + GenAI across different stages of the V-cycle can help accelerate design, improve production readiness, and support system validation, while maintaining the reliability, traceability, and quality required for automotive systems. Another interesting aspect was the changing role of engineers in the age of GenAI. Rather than replacing engineers, AI can help them move up the value chain by automating well-defined implementation tasks and reducing repetitive work, allowing engineers to focus more on system thinking, design decisions, and solving complex engineering problems. The future is not AI replacing engineering, it is AI enhancing engineering. #GenAI #AutomotiveEngineering #ModelBasedDesign #MATLAB #Simulink https://lnkd.in/ekxrD6Fx
